verdict.rationale: dlt pipelines are plain Python code using decorators/config (dlt.pipeline, dlt.resource) that run anywhere Python runs (laptop, Airflow, Lambda, containers), making them naturally versionable and portable in a normal repo; a community adopter explicitly praises this code-first, git-friendly workflow ('I can do everything via code, which makes things more maintainable'), and docs show simple deployment via GitHub Actions/CI. missing for 10: no direct documentation of code review workflows or repo structure conventions, and dltHub's managed/hosted deploy option is a slight counterpoint to pure self-hosted portability though core OSS library remains code-first.
